experiment: E3: streaming reduce (no (rows,tile) fp32 fragment) against the vendor
card: npu:1 (no processes reported, but high power/temperature; vendor absolute unstable this session)
method: msprof per-kernel device time, vendor bracketed in the same window
caveat: vendor absolute moved 0.051-0.092 ms across this session on the shared card; only within-window comparisons are valid
conclusion: removing the (rows,tile) fp32 fragment and reducing straight from shared, reading x_ub twice, is 60-66% SLOWER (0.263-0.273 ms vs the 0.164 ms fragment-based baseline). The fp32 fragment is not the overhead; it is the better data path. rows=8 with 3 versions again overflows UB.
decision: KEEP none; REVERT. Together with E1 (deeper prefetch flat) this exhausts the cheap data-path knobs: the ~3x gap is structural. Closing it needs a genuinely different design (e.g. a vendor-like layout using L1 or a different reduction/vectorisation), not tile/prefetch/fragment tweaks.
